_about: Hand-scored parts of the hunt-2 scorecard (reports/hunt2_prereg.md). Mechanism and implementability were scored on Nov 8 2026 (ET) after the ten builders started and before any idea was frozen or any HOLD read; the other hand-scored parts (realism, neighbours, divers, capacity) are added after the builds, from DEV quantities and the build reports. Sub-scores: mechanism = named forced/eager counterparty (0-4) + evidence it persists (0-3: 3 = documented in crypto in more than one period by independent work, 2 = documented in other markets or in one crypto study, 1 = theory or anecdote) + capacity-limited so big funds pass (0-3); implement = inputs live in the US (0-4) + Coinbase order types (0-3) + low operational complexity (0-3).

who.mechanism_why: 4: forced sellers (liquidation engines, stops, retail panic) vs informed blocks/metaorders, named with the reason each trades. 2: Kyle/Glosten-Milgrom and stealth-trading evidence in equities; crypto microstructure measures predict (Easley et al.), but no crypto study of pre-fill composition. 3: a filter on the incumbent's small-capacity niche.
who.implement_why: 4: Coinbase public trade feed. 3: cancel a resting post-only bid. 2: rolling 30-minute print features for 17 coins in the bot's loop.

exh.mechanism_why: 4: liquidation engines sell until their queue is empty (front-loaded). 2: one crypto study of the Oct 10 2025 cascade (Garcia Seuma 2026). 3: filter on the incumbent's niche.
exh.implement_why: 4: Coinbase trade feed. 3: cancel bids. 2: EWMA intensity and cumulative-selling state per coin.

mac.mechanism_why: 3: informed traders at scheduled releases (adverse selection), named but not forced. 3: CPI and FOMC effects on BTC documented by several studies 2022-26. 3: filter on the incumbent's niche.
mac.implement_why: 4: official calendars. 3: cancel bids. 3: a static schedule.

burn.mechanism_why: 3: a persistent informed seller, inferred from our own failed fill rather than observed. 2: metaorder long memory (Bouchaud et al., Donier-Bonart on BTC) and ladder v6's in-sample remainder drift. 3: filter on the incumbent's niche.
burn.implement_why: 4: the bot's own fills. 3: cancel bids. 3: a per-coin timer.

shape.mechanism_why: 3: liquidation air pockets vs a metaorder's grind, inferred from the path. 2: BTC negative jumps recover (Scaillet-Treccani-Trevisan 2020); lasting impact from persistent flow (Donier-Bonart). 3: filter on the incumbent's niche.
shape.implement_why: 4: Coinbase candles. 3: cancel bids. 3: four candle features.

imp.mechanism_why: 4: forced flow (impact relaxes) vs quote revision on information (impact stays), with a quantitative law. 2: the square-root law is documented on BTC (Donier-Bonart 2015); the informed-impact permanence evidence is from equities (Farmer et al. 2013). 3: filter on the incumbent's niche.
imp.implement_why: 4: Coinbase trades and candles. 3: cancel bids. 2: signed-flow windows, daily volatility and beta in the loop.

crowd.mechanism_why: 4: exchange liquidation engines (crowded longs) vs voluntary sellers. 2: liquidation cascades after long crowding are documented across several crypto episodes, but funding as a filter for intraday reversals is untested. 3: filter on the incumbent's niche.
crowd.implement_why: 3: Hyperliquid's public info API is reachable from the US for data, but it is an offshore venue US persons cannot trade, so access could change. 3: cancel bids. 3: one daily value per coin.

gamma.mechanism_why: 4: option dealers hedging (short gamma sells into falls). 2: documented in equity index futures (Baltussen et al. 2021; Pearson-Poteshman-White 2006); crypto evidence is practitioner-level. 3: filter on the incumbent's niche.
gamma.implement_why: 3: Deribit public market data is reachable from the US (Deribit itself is not open to US persons). 3: cancel bids. 1: a live dealer inventory rebuilt from every option trade since listing, with errors that accumulate.

letf.mechanism_why: 4: leveraged-ETF issuers must trade AUM x L(L-1) x r into the 4 pm reference. 2: documented in equity LETFs (Cheng-Madhavan 2009; Ivanov-Lenkey 2014; Shum et al. 2016); crypto LETFs are young. 1: the flow is public and large, so fast funds and the ETFs' own APs compete for it.
letf.implement_why: 4: ETF data and Coinbase/CFM feeds. 3: CFM perp market and limit orders on Coinbase Advanced. 2: a timed daily routine on exchange holidays and early closes.

exp.mechanism_why: 4: dealers unwinding expiring hedges in Deribit's 08:00 UTC TWAP window. 1: expiry pinning and unwind effects are documented in equities; crypto evidence is anecdotal. 1: dealers know their own inventory better than any outsider and trade the window themselves.
exp.implement_why: 3: Deribit public data reachable from the US. 3: CFM perps on Coinbase Advanced. 1: dealer inventory reconstruction plus a weekly 04:00 ET routine.
